NO NEW IAEA DEVELOPMENT DATED 18 JULY 2026 WAS FOUND. Status as of early/mid July 2026:

- IAEA inspectors have not yet returned to Iran's nuclear facilities. The agency believes Iran's stockpile of enriched uranium remains at the sites.
- Grossi said the IAEA had requested access to the facilities but had not yet received permission to return, and expressed hope inspectors could return within the coming weeks.
- The IAEA has been allowed to visit other nuclear sites in Iran since the 12-day war, such as the Bushehr nuclear power plant, but without access to the enrichment sites it cannot verify the status of Iran's stockpile or check the centrifuge cascades.

DIRECT QUOTE - Rafael Grossi, IAEA Director General (late June 2026), on the US-Iran memorandum of understanding: the MoU stated "explicitly" that "nuclear activities that are going to be carried out with regards to nuclear material facilities will be supervised by the IAEA".

DIRECT QUOTE - Rafael Grossi, IAEA Director General, on timing of inspections (24 June 2026):
"Whether this happens the day after tomorrow or in one week or in 10 days, it's important, but not essential. This is going to happen."

DIRECT QUOTE - Kazem Gharibabadi, Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister (late June 2026): these issues would only be reviewed and decided within the framework of a final agreement and as a result of practical action by the other side to end all sanctions. (paraphrase as carried in reporting)

CONTEXT: The MoU signed by Iran and the US provided a 60-day period to reach a comprehensive agreement covering the nuclear issue, freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, and territorial integrity issues related to the ceasefire.
